name: White-throated Robin
rangeDescription: Türkiye, southern caucasus, and levant eastward to iran, and from southern kazakhstan and tajikistan to western and northern afghanistan; possibly also central uzbekistan; winters in northeastern and eastern africa
description: Large, long-billed robin that spends much of its time on the ground with tail cocked. The male has bluish upperparts, a dark face, a white supercilium, a broad black tail, and bright orange underparts.

name: Crimson-fronted Parakeet
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southeastern nicaragua, costa rica, and western panama
description: Mostly green with long, pointed tail. Red forehead.

name: New Zealand Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: New zealand (little barrier island)
description: Small seabird endemic to New Zealand. Dark blackish-brown head, breast, upperparts, and tail.

name: Taiwan Yuhina
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: A small, tit-like endemic songbird, brown above, white below, with a very distinctive head pattern: the pointed crest is white with a black-bordered chestnut front, and the ear coverts are outlined in black on the white face. Inhabits hilly and montane forests, where it roams about in large chattering flocks at all levels of the forest.

name: Scimitar-winged Piha
rangeDescription: Southern peru (cordillera apolobamba of puno) and western bolivia
description: Rare cotinga found along the east slope of the Andes in Bolivia and southern Peru. Plumage is mostly gray with chestnut flanks and rump.

name: Amazon Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Southern mexico to colombia, venezuela, and east of andes to argentina
description: Medium-sized kingfisher of tropical lowlands. Found singly or in pairs, along rivers and at the edges of ponds and lakes, often perched on wires or bare snags.

name: Broad-billed Prion
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off new zealand and tristan da cunha group
description: The largest of the six prion species, with an exceptionally wide bill that gives the head a chunky appearance. Occurs in dispersed flocks at sea, where it catches prey items either sitting on the water or skimming the surface for zooplankton.

name: Javan Robin
rangeDescription: Mountains of java
description: Medium-sized robin of Java’s montane and foothill forests. Male is dark blue, with a bright white spot on the forehead.

name: Pardusco
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (san martín, la libertad, and huánuco)
description: An odd, warbler-like bird found near treeline in the Andes of northern and central Peru. Pardusco means “brownish” in Spanish, and that fits the bird very well.

name: Rusty-tailed Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Uzbekistan, tajikistan and eastern afghanistan to northern india and nepal
description: Medium-sized brown flycatcher with an orangish tail. Note upright posture and broad-based pale bill.

name: Ivory Gull
rangeDescription: Arctic circumpolar (mainly associated with ice pack)
description: A spectacular and highly sought-after Arctic gull. Unmistakable in all plumages.

name: Santa Marta Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Small, mouse-like bird found in cloud forest understory in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Adult male is gray with a white crown patch and rusty barring on the lower underparts.

name: Yellow-winged Cacique
rangeDescription: Pacific lowlands of western mexico (southeastern sonora) to southeastern guatemala
description: Spectacular and conspicuous black-and-yellow bird of tropical lowlands in west Mexico. Favors deciduous forest and edges, plantations, and hedges with tall trees; often in towns and villages, especially near streams and rivers.

name: Moltoni's Warbler
rangeDescription: Western mediterranean islands, including balearics, corsica, and sardinia
description: Closely related to Eastern and Western Subalpine Warblers. Paler rufous below compared to the Western Subalpine Warbler and lacks contrast between the rusty throat and whitish belly like the Eastern Subalpine Warbler.

name: Hook-billed Bulbul
rangeDescription: Lowland forest of borneo, eastern sumatra, and bangka island
description: A highly localized species, found almost exclusively in the kerangas and peatswamp forests of Borneo and Sumatra’s lowlands (rarely in adjacent wooded habitats). Fairly plain overall; note brown upperparts, off-white chest, pale yellow belly, and elegant white eyebrow.

name: Swamp Greenbul
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to cameroon, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and western uganda
description: A loud, boisterous greenbul that is dark gray-green above and pale below. The back, head, and cheeks are all brownish, but feathers on the head have white centers that give them a distinctly grizzled appearance.

name: Knysna Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Coastal southern south africa (western cape eastward to far southern kwazulu-natal)
description: A furtive woodpecker with densely spotted underparts and face. The male has a reddish crown and moustache; the female has a faint dark moustache and dark crown marked red only toward the back of the head.

name: Vanuatu Megapode
rangeDescription: Forest of vanuatu including banks islands
description: A large-bodied, small-headed, long-legged, mostly ground-dwelling bird. Easily identified by long bright yellowish legs, bright red face, entirely black round body, and bright orange bill.

name: Akikiki
rangeDescription: Montane ohia forest of kauai
description: A small, very rare Hawaiian honeycreeper of remote native forests on Kauai. Declining rapidly; found only above 4,000 feet elevation in the eastern ‘Alaka’i Plateau.

name: Pygmy Batis
rangeDescription: Arid southern ethiopia, sudan, somalia, and kenya to far northeastern tanzania
description: A small batis with typical black, white, and gray markings. Note the chest band, which is black in males and rufous in females.
